docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Minutes

Sync worklogs between multiple time trackers, invoicing, and bookkeeping software. Bug report · Feature request

Charging by the hour is one of the most common ways to invoice a client. Some companies or clients specify the time tracking tool to use, though it usually won't fit your own workflows. This even gets more complicated and cumbersome, when the invoices should contain the tasks you spent time on.

Minutes is a CLI tool, primarily made for entrepreneurs and finance people, to help their daily work by synchronizing worklogs from a source to a target software. The source can be your own time tracking tool you use, let's say Tempo, while the target is a bookkeeping software, like Zoho Books.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
Some features may vary depending on the source and target. For more information, please refer to their documentation.

  • Customize the date time format used for fetching entries
  • Set a specific start and end date to query entries
  • Force every second spent to be billable1
  • Treat tags attached to an entry as tasks you spent time on2
  • Round billable and unbillable seconds to the closest minute per entry3
  • Customizable table output before uploading

For usage examples and configuration options, please check the Getting Started and Configuration documentation.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
The following platforms and tools are supported. If you miss your favorite tool, please send a pull request with the implementation, or file a new feature request.

Tool Use as source Use as target Clockify yes upon request Everhour upon request upon request FreshBooks upon request planned Harvest yes upon request QuickBooks upon request upon request Tempo yes yes Time Doctor upon request upon request TimeCamp upon request upon request Timewarrior yes upon request Toggl Track yes upon request Zoho Books upon request planned

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.3.x
docs.text: If you are moving from the Go-based 0.3.x releases, update your .minutes.toml using the 0.3 → 0.4 migration guide.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: Minutes adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
Warning

Minutes comes with absolutely no warranty. When money comes into the picture, everyone should be more careful what they are doing. Before and after synchronizing any logs to the target, make sure the entries displayed on the screen matching the source entries.

  1. It can be useful if the source does not support billable time, while the target does. ↩

  2. When you need to split time across entries or your source tool does not support tasks, it comes handy to tag entries. ↩

  3. Rounding rules are the following: if you spent >=30 seconds on a task, it will be treated as 1 minute, otherwise 0 (zero). ↩

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little helps, and credit will always be given. You can contribute in many ways.

docs.title: Report Bugs
docs.text:
Report bugs at https://github.com/gabor-boros/minutes/issues.

If you are reporting a bug, please use the bug report template, and include:

  • your operating system name and version
  • any details about your local setup that might be helpful in troubleshooting
  • detailed steps to reproduce the bug

docs.title: Fix Bugs
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for bugs. Anything tagged with "bug" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

docs.title: Implement Features
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for features. Anything tagged with "enhancement" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it. In case you added a new source or target, do not forget to add them to the docs as well.

docs.title: Write Documentation
docs.text: Minutes could always use more documentation, whether as part of the docs, in docstrings, or even on the web in blog posts, articles, and such.

docs.title: Submit Feedback
docs.text:
The best way to send feedback is to file an issue.

If you are proposing a feature:

  • explain in detail how it would work
  • keep the scope as narrow as possible, to make it easier to implement
  • remember that this is a volunteer-driven project, and that contributions are welcome :)

docs.title: Get Started!
docs.text:
Ready to contribute? Here's how to set up minutes for local development.

As step 0 make sure you have mise installed.

  1. Fork the repository
  2. Clone your fork locally
$ git clone git@github.com:your_name_here/minutes.git
  1. Install tools and hooks
$ cd minutes
$ mise trust
$ mise install
$ mise run pre-commit
$ mise run docs:deps
  1. Create a branch for local development
$ git checkout -b github-username/bugfix-or-feature-name
  1. When you're done making changes, check that your changes are formatted, passing linters, and tests are succeeding
$ mise run format
$ mise run lint
$ mise run test
  1. Update documentation and check the results by running mise run docs
  2. Commit your changes and push your branch to GitHub

We use conventional commits. Commit messages are checked by commitlint via the commit-msg hook.

$ git add .
$ git commit -m "feat(scope): summary"
$ git push origin github-username/bugfix-or-feature-name
  1. Submit a pull request on GitHub

docs.title: Pull Request Guidelines
docs.text:
Before you submit a pull request, check that it meets these guidelines:

  1. The pull request should include tests
  2. Tests should pass for the PR
  3. If the pull request adds new functionality, or changes existing one, the docs should be updated

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
A reminder for the maintainers on how to release.

Releases are driven by Release Please. Conventional commits on main open or update a release PR that bumps [workspace.package].version in the root Cargo.toml (member crates inherit via version.workspace = true) and updates CHANGELOG.md. The config uses release-type: simple because the rust strategy cannot rewrite inherited member versions.

  1. Make sure every required PR is merged
  2. Make sure CI is green on main
  3. Wait for (or trigger) the Release Please PR
  4. Review the changelog and version bump, then merge the Release Please PR
  5. Merging creates the GitHub Release/tag; the release workflow builds multi-platform binaries, uploads them to the release, and updates the Homebrew formula in gabor-boros/homebrew-brew

docs.title: Maintainer secrets
docs.text:
Configure these repository secrets for CI:

  • HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN — token with write access to gabor-boros/homebrew-brew
  • Optionally a PAT for Release Please if the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot open release PRs

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This page documents the available settings for minutes. Please note that not all configuration options are covered by a CLI flag.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Minutes looks for the configuration file in the following places, based on your operating system.

The configuration file name in every case is .minutes.toml.

docs.title: Linux/Unix
docs.text:
• $HOME/.minutes.toml
  • $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.minutes.toml as specified by https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html

docs.title: Darwin
docs.text:
• $HOME/.minutes.toml
  • $HOME/Library/Application Support/.minutes.toml

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
• %USERPROFILE%/.minutes.toml
  • %AppData%/.minutes.toml

You can also pass an explicit path with --config PATH.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
After the config file is loaded, MINUTES_* environment variables override matching keys. Kebab-case config keys map to uppercase names with underscores:

  • toggl-api-token → MINUTES_TOGGL_API_TOKEN
  • source → MINUTES_SOURCE
  • round-to-closest-minute → MINUTES_ROUND_TO_CLOSEST_MINUTE

Precedence: CLI flags > environment > .minutes.toml > defaults.

docs.title: Common configuration
docs.text:
Config option Kind Description Example Available options date-format string Chrono strftime pattern for start / end date-format = "%Y-%m-%d" dry-run bool Fetch entries from source, print them, but do not upload dry-run = true yes bool Skip the interactive confirmation prompt yes = true end string End date for fetching entries (must match date-format) end = "2021-10-01" filter-client string Regex of the client name to filter for filter-client = '^ACME Inc.?(orporation)$' filter-project string Regex of the project name to filter for filter-project = '.(website).' force-billed-duration bool Treat the total spent time as billable time force-billed-duration = true round-to-closest-minute bool Round time to closest minute, even if the closest minute is 0 (zero) round-to-closest-minute = true source string Fetch source name source = "tempo" clockify, harvest, tempo, timewarrior, toggl start string Start date for fetching entries (must match date-format) start = "2021-10-01" table-hide-column []string Hide the specified columns of the printed overview table table-hide-column = ["start", "end"] summary, project, client, start, end table-sort-by []string Sort the printed table by the given column; each option can have a - prefix for descending sort table-sort-by = ["start", "task"] task, summary, project, client, start, end, billable, unbillable target string Upload target name target = "tempo" Check the list of available targets tags-as-tasks-regex string Regex of the task pattern tags-as-tasks-regex = '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'

Per-backend user IDs use dedicated keys such as clockify-user, harvest-user, toggl-user, and tempo-worker (see source/target docs). There is no generic source-user / target-user.

docs.title: Source and target specific configuration
docs.text: Source and target specific configuration is not covered by this guide. For more information, please refer to the source or target documentation.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
source = "clockify"
target = "tempo"

clockify-url = "https://api.clockify.me/api/v1/"
clockify-api-key = "<clockify API token>"
clockify-workspace = "<clockify workspace ID>"
clockify-user = "<clockify user ID>"

tempo-url = "https://<org>.atlassian.net/"
tempo-username = "<jira username>"
tempo-password = "<jira password or API token>"
tempo-worker = "<jira username>"

tags-as-tasks-regex = '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'
round-to-closest-minute = true
force-billed-duration = true

filter-client = '^ACME Inc\.?(orporation)$'
filter-project = '.*(website).*'

table-sort-by = [
    "start",
    "project",
    "task",
    "summary",
]

table-hide-column = [
    "end"
]

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Minutes is a CLI tool, primarily made for entrepreneurs and finance people, to help their daily work by synchronizing worklogs from a source to a target software. The source can be your own time tracking tool you use, while the target is a bookkeeping software.

This guide shows you the basics of minutes, walks through the available flags, and gives some examples for basic configuration. For the full list of available configuration options, visit the related documentation.

Upgrading from 0.3.x? Read the 0.3 → 0.4 migration guide.

docs.title: Using brew
docs.text:
$ brew tap gabor-boros/brew
$ brew install minutes

docs.title: Manual install
docs.text:
To install minutes, use one of the release artifacts. If you have a Rust toolchain installed, you can build from source as well:

$ cargo install --path crates/minutes-cli

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: minutes has numerous flags and there will be more when other sources or targets are added. Therefore, minutes comes with a config file, that can be placed in the user's home directory or the config directory.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Usage: minutes [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <PATH>                          Path to a `.minutes.toml` file
  -s, --source <SOURCE>                        Source time tracker [clockify|harvest|tempo|timewarrior|toggl]
  -t, --target <TARGET>                        Target time tracker
      --start <START>                          Inclusive range start (must match `--date-format`)
      --end <END>                              Inclusive range end (must match `--date-format`)
      --date-format <FORMAT>                   Chrono strftime pattern (default %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)
      --dry-run                                Fetch and print entries without uploading
      --yes                                    Skip the interactive "Continue?" confirmation
      --force-billed-duration                  Treat total time as billable before upload
      --round-to-closest-minute                Round each entry's duration to the closest minute
      --tags-as-tasks-regex <REGEX>            Regex of tags that should become tasks
      --filter-client <REGEX>                  Regex filter applied to client names after fetch
      --filter-project <REGEX>                 Regex filter applied to project names after fetch
      --table-sort-by <COLUMN>...              Sort overview table by these columns
      --table-hide-column <COLUMN>...          Hide these columns from the overview table
      --clockify-url <URL>                     Clockify API base URL
      --clockify-api-key <KEY>                 Clockify API key
      --clockify-workspace <ID>                Clockify workspace ID
      --clockify-user <ID>                     Clockify user ID
      --harvest-access-token <TOKEN>           Harvest personal access token
      --harvest-account <ID>                   Harvest account ID
      --harvest-user <ID>                      Harvest user ID
      --tempo-url <URL>                        Tempo base URL
      --tempo-username <USER>                  Tempo username for Basic Auth
      --tempo-password <PASSWORD>              Tempo password or API token
      --tempo-worker <WORKER>                  Tempo worker key
      --timewarrior-command <PROGRAM>          Timewarrior executable
      --timewarrior-arguments <ARG>...         Extra Timewarrior arguments
      --timewarrior-unbillable-tag <TAG>       Unbillable tag (default unbillable)
      --timewarrior-client-tag-regex <REGEX>   Client tag regex
      --timewarrior-project-tag-regex <REGEX>  Project tag regex
      --toggl-url <URL>                        Toggl Track API base URL
      --toggl-api-token <TOKEN>                Toggl API token
      --toggl-workspace <ID>                   Toggl workspace ID
      --toggl-user <ID>                        Toggl user ID
  -h, --help                                   Print help

docs.title: Usage examples
docs.text: Depending on the config file, the number of flags can change.

docs.title: Simplest command
docs.text:
# No arguments, no flags, just running the command
$ minutes

docs.title: Preview without uploading
docs.text: $ minutes --dry-run

docs.title: Non-interactive sync
docs.text: $ minutes --yes

docs.title: Set specific date and time
docs.text:
$ minutes --start "2021-10-07 00:00:00" --end "2021-10-07 23:59:59"

$ minutes --date-format "%Y-%m-%d" --start "2021-10-07" --end "2021-10-08"

docs.title: Use tags for tasks
docs.text: $ minutes --tags-as-tasks-regex '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'

docs.title: Minute based rounding
docs.text: $ minutes --round-to-closest-minute

docs.title: Format the table output
docs.text: $ minutes --table-sort-by "-start" --table-hide-column "client" --table-hide-column "project"

docs.title: Config file vs flags
docs.text:
Be aware that not all configuration options are covered by flags, especially advanced options.

When using the configuration file and flags in conjunction, flags take precedence over environment variables and the configuration file.

docs.title: Migrating from 0.3.x to 0.4.x
docs.text: Minutes 0.4.x is a Rust rewrite of the 0.3.x Go CLI. The binary name, brew tap, and overall workflow are the same, but .minutes.toml keys and date formats changed. Update your config before syncing real data, and run with --dry-run first.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Install from the same places as before:

brew tap gabor-boros/brew
brew install minutes

Or download a release artifact from GitHub Releases. Building from source now requires a Rust toolchain (cargo install --path crates/minutes-cli) instead of Go.

docs.title: Date format
docs.text:
date-format no longer uses Go reference layouts. It uses chrono strftime patterns.

0.3.x (Go) 0.4.x (chrono) 2006-01-02 15:04:05 %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S 2006-01-02 %Y-%m-%d 15:04:05 %H:%M:%S

Default in 0.4.x is %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.

docs.title: User IDs: source-user / target-user removed
docs.text:
Generic source-user and target-user are gone. Set the user (or worker) on the backend that needs it:

0.3.x 0.4.x Notes source-user (Clockify) clockify-user source-user (Harvest) harvest-user source-user (Toggl) toggl-user source-user (Tempo) tempo-worker Worker key for search/create; still use tempo-username for auth target-user (Tempo) tempo-worker Same worker key when Tempo is the target source-user = "-" (Timewarrior) (remove) Timewarrior has no user id

docs.title: Renamed keys
docs.text: 0.3.x 0.4.x toggl-api-key toggl-api-token harvest-api-key harvest-access-token

docs.title: Removed keys
docs.text:
These go-pretty table options have no equivalent in 0.4.x; delete them from your config:

  • table-column-config (and nested [table-column-config.*] tables)
  • table-column-truncates / table-truncate-column

table-sort-by and table-hide-column still work.

docs.title: Unchanged keys
docs.text: These keep the same names: source, target, start, end, dry-run, force-billed-duration, round-to-closest-minute, tags-as-tasks-regex, filter-client, filter-project, table-sort-by, table-hide-column, plus existing Clockify / Tempo / Timewarrior URL and credential fields that already matched (clockify-api-key, tempo-url, tempo-username, tempo-password, timewarrior-*, and so on).

docs.title: New options
docs.text:
• yes / --yes — skip the interactive "Continue?" confirmation
  • Environment overrides with a MINUTES_ prefix: kebab-case config keys map to MINUTES_ + underscores (for example toggl-api-token → MINUTES_TOGGL_API_TOKEN, source → MINUTES_SOURCE)

Configuration precedence: CLI flags > MINUTES_* env > .minutes.toml > defaults.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
1. Rewrite date-format to chrono strftime (or remove it to use the default).
  2. Replace source-user / target-user with the per-backend keys above.
  3. Rename toggl-api-key and harvest-api-key if you use those sources.
  4. Delete table-column-config / truncate settings.
  5. Run minutes --dry-run and confirm the overview table before uploading.

docs.title: Clockify
docs.text: Source documentation for Clockify.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
The source makes the following special mappings.

From To Description Tags Task Turns tags into tasks and splits the entry into as many pieces as the item has matching tags when tags-as-tasks-regex is set Task Summary or Description Tasks are used for the summary of an entry; when tags-as-tasks-regex is set, Summary is set to the Description of the item

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
Flags:
    --clockify-api-key <KEY>       Clockify API key
    --clockify-url <URL>           Clockify API base URL (default https://api.clockify.me/api/v1/)
    --clockify-workspace <ID>      Clockify workspace ID
    --clockify-user <ID>           Clockify user ID

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text: Config option Kind Description Example clockify-url string Clockify API base URL clockify-url = "https://api.clockify.me/api/v1/" clockify-api-key string API key gathered from Clockify<sup>1</sup> clockify-api-key = "" clockify-workspace string Clockify workspace ID<sup>2</sup> clockify-workspace = "" clockify-user string Clockify user ID clockify-user = ""

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: No known limitations.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
source = "clockify"
target = "tempo"

clockify-url = "https://api.clockify.me/api/v1/"
clockify-api-key = "<YOUR API KEY>"
clockify-workspace = "<YOUR WORKSPACE ID>"
clockify-user = "<YOUR USER ID>"

tempo-url = "https://<org>.atlassian.net/"
tempo-username = "<jira username>"
tempo-password = "<jira password or API token>"
tempo-worker = "<jira username>"

tags-as-tasks-regex = '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'
round-to-closest-minute = true
force-billed-duration = true

  1. As described in the API documentation, visit the settings page to get your API token. ↩

  2. To get your workspace ID, navigate to workspace settings and copy the ID from the URL. ↩

docs.title: Harvest
docs.text: Source documentation for Harvest.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
The source makes the following special mappings.

From To Description Notes Notes, Summary Notes are mapped to both notes and summary as that was the most meaningful option

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
Flags:
    --harvest-account <ID>              Harvest account ID
    --harvest-access-token <TOKEN>      Harvest personal access token
    --harvest-user <ID>                 Harvest user ID

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text: Config option Kind Description Example harvest-account int The account ID where the token belongs harvest-account = 123456789 harvest-access-token string Personal access token gathered from Harvest<sup>1</sup> harvest-access-token = "" harvest-user string Harvest user ID harvest-user = ""

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • Harvest does not support tags which makes it impossible to get tasks from tags. A workaround is planned.

docs.title: Timewarrior
docs.text:
Source documentation for Timewarrior.

Timewarrior is one of the most flexible tools. Thanks to its flexibility there is no built-in/dedicated way to mark an entry billable/unbillable, set client, project, or task.

Therefore, several assumptions were made to integrate with Timewarrior, though the goal was to keep the maximum flexibility.

Warning

Timewarrior has no built-in support for marking an entry billable/unbillable. Therefore, every entry will be treated as billable unless it is forced by force-billed-duration or a matching tag for timewarrior-unbillable-tag.

Warning

When timewarrior-client-tag-regex or timewarrior-project-tag-regex is matching multiple tags, the last tag will be used.

Warning

To extract tasks from tags, set the tags-as-tasks-regex.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
The source makes the following special mappings.

From To Description Annotation Notes, Summary, Task (optionally) Annotations are used to set Notes and Summary; if no task regex is set, it will be used for Task as well Tags Client, Project, Task Depending on the client, project, and task regex, tags will be used accordingly

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
Flags:
    --timewarrior-arguments <ARG>...           Extra arguments prepended to every Timewarrior invocation
    --timewarrior-client-tag-regex <REGEX>     Regex matching tags treated as the client
    --timewarrior-command <PROGRAM>            Executable name or path (default timew)
    --timewarrior-project-tag-regex <REGEX>    Regex matching tags treated as the project
    --timewarrior-unbillable-tag <TAG>         Tag that marks an interval as non-billable (default unbillable)

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text: Config option Kind Description Example timewarrior-arguments []string Extra arguments for Timewarrior timewarrior-arguments = ["log"] timewarrior-client-tag-regex string Regex for extracting Client names from tags timewarrior-client-tag-regex = '^(CLIENT-\w+)$' timewarrior-command string Timewarrior command timewarrior-command = "timew" timewarrior-project-tag-regex string Regex for extracting Project names from tags timewarrior-project-tag-regex = '^PROJ-DEV-\w+$' timewarrior-unbillable-tag string Tag that marks entries as unbillable timewarrior-unbillable-tag = "unbillable"

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: No known limitations.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
source = "timewarrior"
target = "tempo"

timewarrior-arguments = ["log"]
timewarrior-client-tag-regex = '^(oc)$'
timewarrior-project-tag-regex = '^(log)$'

tempo-url = "https://<org>.atlassian.net/"
tempo-username = "<jira username>"
tempo-password = "<jira password or API token>"
tempo-worker = "<jira username>"

tags-as-tasks-regex = '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'
round-to-closest-minute = true
force-billed-duration = true

docs.title: Toggl Track
docs.text:
Source documentation for Toggl Track.

Warning

To get the available User IDs, please follow this instruction. Only workspace admins can get the User IDs.

Info

Toggl Track's detailed report API does support filtering, and minutes supports filtering by setting toggl-user to the desired user ID.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
The source makes the following special mappings.

From To Description Description Summary Toggl Track has no separate notes field for entries in this integration

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
Flags:
    --toggl-api-token <TOKEN>    Toggl API token
    --toggl-url <URL>            Toggl Track API base URL (default https://api.track.toggl.com/)
    --toggl-workspace <ID>       Toggl workspace ID
    --toggl-user <ID>            Toggl user ID

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text: Config option Kind Description Example toggl-api-token string API token gathered from Toggl Track<sup>1</sup> toggl-api-token = "" toggl-url string Toggl Track API base URL toggl-url = "https://api.track.toggl.com/" toggl-workspace int Workspace ID toggl-workspace = 123456789 toggl-user string User ID toggl-user = ""

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • No precise start and end date filtering is accepted by Toggl Track report API that is used for this source, therefore only ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) date format can be used. Set date-format = "%Y-%m-%d" when using day-only ranges.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
source = "toggl"
target = "tempo"

# To retrieve your user ID, please follow the instructions listed here:
# https://github.com/toggl/toggl_api_docs/blob/master/chapters/workspaces.md#get-workspace-users
toggl-user = "<YOUR TOGGL USER ID>"
toggl-api-token = "<YOUR API TOKEN>"
toggl-url = "https://api.track.toggl.com/"
toggl-workspace = 123456789

tempo-url = "https://<org>.atlassian.net/"
tempo-username = "<jira username>"
tempo-password = "<jira password or API token>"
tempo-worker = "<jira username>"

tags-as-tasks-regex = '[A-Z]{2,7}-\d{1,6}'
round-to-closest-minute = true
force-billed-duration = true

  1. Visit your Toggl Track profile page to create or copy an API token. ↩

docs.title: Tempo
docs.text:
Target documentation for Tempo.

Warning

Tempo can go crazy when not a whole minute is uploaded. It is highly recommended using the round-to-closest-minute option.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
The target makes the following special mappings.

From To Description Summary Comment The entry summary will be used as the comment Task OriginTaskID Since OriginTaskID must be an Issue Key, the Issue Key defined by Task must exist in Jira tempo-worker Worker Worker key sent on create/search requests

docs.title: CLI flags
docs.text:
Flags:
    --tempo-password <PASSWORD>    Tempo password or API token for Basic Auth
    --tempo-url <URL>              Tempo base URL
    --tempo-username <USER>        Tempo username for Basic Auth
    --tempo-worker <WORKER>        Tempo worker key used on search and create requests

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text: Config option Kind Description Example tempo-password string Jira password or API token tempo-password = "" tempo-url string URL for the Jira installation tempo-url = "https://example.atlassian.net/" tempo-username string Jira username tempo-username = "gabor-boros" tempo-worker string Worker key for search/create tempo-worker = "gabor-boros"

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• It is not possible to filter for projects when fetching, though it is a planned feature.
  • Tempo entries cannot have Summary and Notes at the same time, therefore we use Summary for the comment field during upload.
  • At the moment, it is not possible to upload an entry in the name of someone else beyond setting tempo-worker.
